whatsapp_text: Hi, I'd like to understand how the audit trail works in HIMS.
persona: Hospital administrator or finance head who has had to investigate a disputed entry

sections.h2: What an audit trail is in a hospital system
paras: An audit trail is the hospital's memory of its own actions: a record, kept automatically, of which user created or changed which entry and at what time. In HIMS it runs under registration, the clinical record, the pharmacy, the laboratory, inventory and billing, so a question about a discount, a cancelled bill, a changed result or a late note can be answered from the system rather than from recollection.

The point is not suspicion. It is that a hospital runs on three shifts and dozens of hands, and without attribution every disagreement becomes a matter of who sounds more certain. With it, the conversation starts from a timed entry and a name, and usually ends there.

sections.h2: Four arguments a hospital has every month without a trail.
sections.lead: Each of these is routine, and each is unresolvable when the record cannot say who or when.

items.p: The bill went out lower than the tariff. Without a name against the change, the enquiry stalls and the habit continues.

items.h: A cancelled bill and a missing receipt
items.p: Cash was taken at the counter and the bill later cancelled. The register shows the end state and nothing about the route to it.

items.h: A charge the patient's family disputes
items.p: A consumable or an investigation is questioned at discharge. Somebody retypes the bill from memory instead of reading when the item was added and by whom.
The counter works under a single account, so every entry is attributed to nobody in particular.

sections.h2: Attribution happens because of how people log in, not because of extra work.

steps.p: Each doctor, nurse, pharmacist, technician and counter staff member has their own login rather than a shared one.

steps.h: A role, not a free hand
steps.p: Access is granted by designation, so people reach the screens their job needs and not the rest.

steps.h: Entries stamped as they are made
steps.p: Registration, notes, orders, dispensing, results, charges and receipts all carry the user and the moment.
A correction is recorded as a change to the earlier value, so both states can be read.
A dispute, a claim query or a documentation review is settled by opening the history rather than by asking around.

items.q: What exactly is recorded against an entry?
items.a: The user who made it and the time it was made, held with the entry itself. That applies across registration, clinical notes, orders, dispensing, results, charges and receipts, so an episode can be read as a sequence of attributed actions rather than a final state.

items.q: Can a user delete something to hide a mistake?
items.a: Access is granted by role, so most staff cannot remove records at all, and changes are recorded rather than silently applied. Which roles may amend or cancel what is agreed during scoping, because a small nursing home and a multi-specialty hospital draw that line differently.

items.q: Does this slow the counter down?
items.a: No. The trail is a by-product of people logging in as themselves and doing their normal work. The only real change is giving up shared accounts, which is what makes attribution meaningful in the first place.

items.q: Is this the same thing as NABH documentation?
items.a: It supports it. Accreditation looks for records that are complete, timed and attributed, among many other things. See NABH documentation software for that side, and confirm current standards with the accrediting body and your advisers.

items.q: Does the trail cover imaging as well?
items.a: Yes. Imaging runs through AuraPACS inside HIMS, which has role-based access for radiologists, technicians, front desk and referrers, and study and report activity is audited alongside the rest of the record.

items.q: Can we see activity for one user or one day?
items.a: Activity can be read by patient, by bill, by user or by date range. The views your administrators and finance team need are settled during scoping so the log is useful rather than merely complete.
